Other names: RK45 / Dormand-Prince 5(4) / DOPRI5 / 埋込みRunge–Kutta Read the formulation Read the chapter Assumptions for this example The target is a smooth nonstiff initial-value problem; tolerances must match component scales. FSAL reuses the RHS owned by the accepted state and never promotes a rejected trial endpoint. Simple sign crossings are localized on interpolants of retained accepted steps. Boundaries: The ODE step has no spatial boundary; an RHS for a semidiscrete PDE must supply its boundaries. Units: Time and step size share units; atol has each state component's units and rtol is dimensionless. Small dedicated implementations and measured checks Additional fixed examples: RK45: embedded errors, dense output and events. See each release for assumptions and checked scope. There is no general guarantee for tangential roots, multiple crossings within a step or systems with resets. Initial-zero and ownership controls are limited component tests; local tolerances and global accuracy remain distinct.
